Method of Attack: Deploy remote access trojan (Gh0st RAT variant) on poorly secured Microsoft SQL and MySQL database servers
Use weak account credentials and no oversight to breach servers
Write malicious executable 'mcsql.exe' to disk via mysqld.exe, mysqld-nt.exe, and sqlserver.exe processes
Establish connection with C2 server to receive commands and exfiltrate data
Keylogging using Windows Polling method (GetAsyncKeyState API) to steal user inputs
Persistence via Windows registry modification and self-copy module

Remote commands include downloading payloads, connecting to URLs, destroying MBR, keylogging, stealing clipboard data, collecting Tencent-related info, updating, uninstalling, registering run key, terminating host, rebooting NIC, scanning processes, displaying pop-ups
Attack Vector: Exploitation of poorly secured database servers with weak credentials and no oversight
Indicators of Compromise: Processes mysqld.exe, mysqld-nt.exe, sqlserver.exe used to write malware
Use of Microsoft SQL xp_cmdshell command to drop Cobalt Strike beacons (similar attacks)
